skill.name: memory-management
skill.description: Manage authorized project memory across sessions through HOT, WARM, and COLD notes, with controlled consolidation, archiving, registry reconciliation, and subject erasure.
skill.summary: Maintain authorized project context across sessions without treating working notes as canonical truth.

content.value_statement: Project context becomes stale, duplicated, or disconnected across sessions. This skill organizes authorized notes, preserves source links, and supports controlled archival, reconciliation, and erasure.
actual_capabilities: Initializes authorized project-local memory from templates and confirms runtime data is excluded from Git.
Retrieves current context through HOT pointers, WARM evidence, COLD history, and accepted registry records.
Captures dated notes with sources, observation dates, assumptions, open loops, and registry offsets after permission.
Consolidates duplicate non-canonical notes while preserving conflicts, provenance, and higher-authority records.
Demotes stale HOT notes and archives eligible WARM artifacts with original paths, hashes, and source pointers.
Performs authorized subject erasure across working notes and rendered views while preserving minimal suppression records.
limitations: Requires companion registry scripts and shared references for initialization and canonical fact workflows.
Cannot accept registry proposals or directly change canonical registry facts.
Does not guarantee deletion from Git history, backups, or external systems.
Depends on explicit authorization for persistent writes, promotions, archival changes, and erasure.

use_cases.title: Preserve campaign context
use_cases.description: Keep priorities, metrics, decisions, and evidence pointers available across sessions without treating summaries as canonical truth.

use_cases.title: Reconcile project notes
use_cases.description: Deduplicate comparable findings, preserve conflicts, and flag unsupported conclusions or broken source links.

use_cases.title: Handle an erasure request
use_cases.description: Plan and execute an authorized working-tree purge with suppression checks, minimal logging, and honest scope reporting.

prompt_templates.title: Review current memory
prompt_templates.prompt: Review the authorized project memory for [scope]. Summarize current priorities, source records, stale items, and open questions. Make no changes.

prompt_templates.title: Save a sourced finding
prompt_templates.prompt: Save this authorized finding as a dated WARM note: [finding]. Include the source, observation date, assumptions, open loops, and related registry offset.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a consolidation
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a dry-run consolidation plan for [scope]. Identify exact duplicates, comparable supersessions, conflicts, broken links, and archive candidates. Preserve canonical records.

prompt_templates.title: Perform a controlled purge
prompt_templates.prompt: Prepare and execute an authorized purge for [pseudonymous aggregate ID]. Verify scope, check suppression, minimize logs, rebuild projections, and report remaining retention limits.

output_examples.input: Create a dry-run consolidation plan for keyword research notes.
output: Three notes are exact duplicates and can retain one strongest source pointer.

output_examples.input: Purge the authorized pseudonymous subject from working memory.
output: Suppression was checked before working copies were changed.
Authorized notes and rendered views were anonymized, then projections were rebuilt.
The report does not claim removal from Git history, backups, or external systems.

best_practices: Start with read-only review and request authorization before the first persistent write.
Link HOT summaries to dated evidence or accepted registry records and label stale or estimated facts.
Report every changed path, event identifier, unresolved conflict, and privacy limitation after an operation.
anti_patterns: Do not store credentials, raw contact data, production exports, or large evidence sets in HOT memory.
Do not edit event streams, projections, or approved decisions to make conflicting notes appear consistent.
Do not claim complete erasure when Git history, backups, or external copies remain outside the operation.

faq.question: Can this skill change canonical registry facts?
faq.answer: No. It can submit authorized proposals, but only the owning registry can accept or mutate canonical facts.

faq.question: When does the skill require authorization?
faq.answer: Persistent writes, HOT promotion, archival changes, audit output, and erasure require explicit authorization. Read-only review and dry runs do not.

faq.question: What are HOT, WARM, and COLD memory?
faq.answer: HOT stores brief current pointers, WARM stores dated evidence, and COLD stores historical notes retrieved only when needed.

faq.question: Should runtime memory be committed to Git?
faq.answer: No. Runtime memory, events, projections, audits, exports, and subject records should remain ignored unless a protected governance process exists.

faq.question: Does a purge remove every copy of personal data?
faq.answer: No. The workflow changes authorized working copies and projections, but Git history, backups, and external systems may retain data.

faq.question: Can a standalone one-folder installation initialize registry state?
faq.answer: No. Initialization depends on shared runtime references, registry scripts, schemas, and host capabilities outside this skill folder.
